To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a deep multi-task network with shared layers outperforms single-task networks for attribute classification, and (2) the use of a second network to combine the outputs of the first network can improve the performance of the first network, especially when the two networks are trained together.

(i) using a multi-task convolutional neural network with shared lower layers improves attribute classification performance; (ii) sharing the higher layers of the network for related attributes improves performance; and (iii) building an auxiliary network to improve attribute classification performance by utilizing scores from all other attributes improves performance.
1) a multi-task network can be used to improve the accuracy of attribute classification, and 2) an auxiliary network can be used in conjunction with a multi-task network to further improve accuracy.

the problem of attribute classification.

we show that attributes are not independent and by using a multi task network, the accuracy of attribute classification can be greatly improved.

we can achieve significant improvements in attribute classification by taking advantage of attribute relationships.
